messages:
maria: Heads up — saw a customer hit a busted routing path. Request from their VPC private endpoint arrived with X-Workspace set to ws-A, but X-Pool-Affinity pointed at pool-B (belongs to ws-B). Gateway returned 403. Is that expected?

sam: Wait — do we currently treat the dedicated pool header as authoritative over the vpc endpoint ownership? I thought endpoint binding should win for security.

josh: Implementation today is messy: if via PrivateEndpoint we verify endpoint.owner == workspace header; if mismatch -> reject. For pool header we check pool.tenant == workspace and if not we fall back to shared. But we don't have a clear precedence doc.

li: We should be explicit: precedence matters. My vote: private_endpoint > workspace_header > pool_header for security. If endpoint says it's ws-A, reject claims for ws-B.

olivia: Strong agree on VPC owning the truth. That said, there are legit admin flows where ops attach a different pool header for maintenance. We could allow a controlled override but with audit.

kevin: Also telemetry gap: routing failures here show only 403. We need routing.decision tag and reason codes (vpc_mismatch, pool_mismatch, success_pool_affinity, fallback_shared) so alerts/console can surface why a request didn't route.

maria: Proposed config snippet to be explicit:

```
routing.precedence = ["private_endpoint", "workspace_header", "pool_header"]
routing.ejection_policy = {
  "private_endpoint": "reject",
  "pool_mismatch": "fallback_shared"
}
```

sam: Console UX: ops needs per-request "why" in trace panel. If we add decision_reason telemetry, show a small pill (reason) + link to endpoint ownership record. :eyes:

josh: Also add automatic "possible causes" when ejection happens: wrong header, rotated key, endpoint misbound. Small text + suggested remediation.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for r-routing-v2 on canary (eng-platform). See #eng-releases for status :rocket:

li: One caveat: strict VPC reject will break cross-workspace orchestrations some customers use. We should ship an "audit-only" mode first so org-admins can see failures without enforcement.

olivia: Rollout suggestion: canary (1%) with decision_reason telemetry -> audit-only for 7 days -> strict ejection after we verify no regressions (2 weeks). Also add an org-admin override flag gated behind RBAC and audit logs.

maria: I'll open a short RFC + PR for telemetry + config change and include migration notes. Tagging @sam @josh for UX and console bits.

sam: Thanks — I'll own the UX patch and quick mock for the trace view.
